claims.text: The as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic HEA has a lamellar microstructure containing B2 BCC and L12 FCC phases.
The as-cast alloy has approximately 18% elongation and 750 MPa yield strength at room temperature.
Aging AlCoCrFeNi2.1 between 550 and 750°C produces a ductile-brittle-ductile transition.
The transition is driven by coupled evolution of L12 ordered domains and jagged B2/FCC phase boundaries.
Aging at approximately 600°C produces excessive L12 ordering in the FCC matrix, approaching a stoichiometric Ni3Al ratio.
Excessive L12 ordering significantly increases the antiphase boundary energy.
High antiphase boundary energy restricts dislocation cross-slip.
Restricted cross-slip forces dislocations into planar slip.
Planar slip causes severe stress concentration at serrated or jagged phase boundaries.
Stress concentration at jagged phase boundaries results in brittle failure.
Aging at approximately 750°C reduces the degree of chemical ordering and lowers the antiphase boundary energy.
Aging at approximately 750°C forms ductile transition zones along phase boundaries.
Lower ordering and lower antiphase boundary energy at 750°C permit cross-slip and restore ductility.
The brittle state exhibits intergranular-like fracture along jagged phase boundaries.
The chemical-ordering transition occurs when the L12 ordering parameter exceeds approximately 0.7.
An L12 ordering parameter above approximately 0.7 corresponds to an antiphase-boundary-energy threshold that inhibits cross-slip.
The critical brittle range is 550-650°C, with ductility recovering above 700°C.
The as-cast alloy has low antiphase boundary energy because its FCC matrix is disordered or only partially ordered.
The 600°C-aged sample should contain jagged phase boundaries and planar slip bands as structural signatures of the proposed mechanism.

If simple phase decomposition alone causes brittleness, the 600°C and 750°C samples should show no significant difference in antiphase boundary energy or cross-slip behavior, and jagged boundaries should not be dominant.

contradictions.description: The initial-state field unqualifiedly identifies the FCC constituent as L12, an ordered structure, whereas the baseline allows the same FCC matrix to be disordered. A fully disordered FCC phase would ordinarily not be designated L12; the intended distinction between partially ordered L12 and disordered FCC is not resolved.
